dataset_title: Full-text roadside-grass anaerobic-digestion feed, process and gas observations
source_title: From grass to gas and beyond: Anaerobic digestion as a key enabling technology for a residual grass biorefinery
source_locations: Methods: pilot-scale continuous wet anaerobic digestion
Methods and Results: dry pilot-scale digestion
Methods and Results: large-scale landfill cell
Discussion: potential of roadside grass to feed a residual grass biorefinery
data_basis: Exact transcription of source-specific feed characterization, operating conditions, process observations, pilot/batch gas outcomes and author-calculated values. Experiment, unit, denominator, qualifier and source location are retained per row.
license: No explicit reuse license identified for the accepted manuscript. This file contains factual observations transcribed with attribution; no figures, table images or manuscript text are reproduced.
applicability: Reference-only evidence for Belgian roadside-grass digestion configurations. Feeds, preprocessing, scales, inocula and operating modes are study-specific and are not demonstrated to match GreenHub's protein-depleted residual stream.
limitations: No values are runtime-activated, parameter defaults, or direct GreenHub calibration targets.

Table 1 EPi-test potentials conflict with potentials stated in parts of the Results for the dry pilot and landfill batches; values remain separate by source location and are not averaged or reconciled.
EPi-test values are source-calculated potentials from composition and are not measured reactor yields. Pilot gas yields are separate observations with distinct bases and configurations.
Wet, dry-pilot and landfill observations are not a matched factorial experiment; differences cannot be attributed to a single operating variable.
A complete feed-to-gas mass, carbon, nitrogen or energy balance is unavailable in accessible manuscript text; no unreported values are inferred.
Supporting chart workbooks/raw time series were unavailable with the accepted manuscript; only values explicitly stated in tables or text are transcribed.
Replicate uncertainty is absent for most process observations. Source qualifiers such as approximately, up to and ranges are preserved.
The reported wet-pilot mixing schedule is 90 seconds of mixing per 480-second cycle; 480 seconds is not a measured off-time.
Dry-pilot inoculum ratio basis differs between Methods and Results (fresh mass versus DOM); no common basis is assumed.
curation_note: The DOI identifies the article. The local dataset URN identifies this GreenHub transcription version; it is not an externally registered DOI or persistent identifier.
